title: Introduction to Styles (Writer)
short: Page, paragraph, character, frame, list and table styles in LibreOffice Writer.
lede: Styles are the backbone of Unit 1. Fill Format plus custom styles are the practical.
lens: Theory asks **types of styles** and **why styles beat manual formatting**.
Practical: apply Heading 1/2, create a custom style, use Fill Format.
concepts: **1. A style** is a named collection of formatting. Change the style once, every place it is used updates.
**2. Six categories in Writer:** Paragraph, Character, Page, Frame, List (Numbering), Table.
**3. Styles window:** Sidebar → Styles, or `F11`. Filter: All / Applied / Hierarchical / Custom.
**4. Fill Format mode:** click Fill Format, then click paragraphs to paint the same style quickly.
**5. Updating a style:** format one paragraph as you want → right-click the style → **Update Style**.
**6. New style:** right-click in Styles → **New**. Give a name, set font/indents/spacing, OK.
**7. Load styles** from another document or template: Styles menu → **Load Styles** (overwrite / page / numbering options).
**8. Why styles:** consistent look, faster ToC (Headings), smaller files than direct formatting, easy branding.
steps: 3. Double-click Heading 1 on the title, Heading 2 on subheadings.
4. To copy, click Fill Format and click each target paragraph.
tricks: - Headings must use **Heading styles**, not just Bold 16 pt — otherwise ToC will be empty.
- Character styles change a **few words** inside a paragraph; paragraph styles change the **whole para**.
mistakes: - Building a ToC from manually bolded text.
- Updating the wrong style and changing the whole document by accident.

qa.q: What is a style in Writer? Name any four categories.
qa.a: A named set of formatting that can be reused. Categories: Paragraph, Character, Page, Frame, List, Table.

qa.q: What is Fill Format mode?
qa.a: A Styles-window tool that copies the selected style onto each paragraph (or object) you click, like a format paintbrush.

qa.q: Why should a long report use styles instead of manual formatting?
qa.a: One change updates every heading; ToC can be generated; the look stays consistent; less chance of mixed fonts; templates become reusable.

qa.q: A 20-page report uses Bold 16 pt for titles. The examiner wants Heading 1 in navy. What should the student do instead of selecting each title?
qa.a: Create or modify **Heading 1** (navy, size, spacing), then Fill Format / select each title and apply Heading 1. Later, one modify updates all.

qa.q:
Read and answer:

Neha’s ToC is empty even though titles look big and bold.

(a) Why?
(b) Steps to fix it.
(c) How will this help next time she changes the colour of all headings?
a: (a) Titles used direct formatting, not Heading styles.
(b) Apply Heading 1/2, then Insert → Table of Contents.
(c) Modify Heading 1 once — every heading and the ToC pick up the new colour.

title: Working with Images (Writer)
short: Insert, wrap, arrange, drawing objects, grouping and captions.
lede: Practical-heavy. Wrap settings and grouping are the viva favourites.
lens: Expect “how to wrap an image” and “difference between anchor types”.
File work: insert a picture, wrap Optimal, add a caption, group a callout.
concepts: **1. Insert image:** Insert → Image, or drag from a folder, or copy-paste. Keep a copy of the picture with the file if you must move the document.
**2. Anchoring:** To Paragraph (moves with that para), To Character, As Character (like a big letter in the line), To Page (stays on that page).
**3. Text wrap:** None, Before, After, Parallel, Optimal, Through, In Background. **Optimal** is the usual body-text wrap.
**4. Arrangement:** Bring to Front / Send to Back when images overlap.
**5. Drawing toolbar:** lines, arrows, rectangles, callouts, text boxes. Hold Shift for a circle/square.
**6. Grouping:** select several drawing objects (Shift-click) → right-click → **Group**. They move as one.
**7. Crop, resize, rotate** from the Image toolbar. Keep aspect ratio unless the question says otherwise.
**8. Caption:** right-click image → Insert Caption (Figure 1: …). Captions help a Table of Figures.
steps: 2. Click the image → Properties / Wrap → Optimal.
5. Add an arrow from Drawing; Shift-select + Group.
tricks: - If text jumps wildly, the image is probably **As Character** — change wrap and anchor.
- Grouping works on **drawing objects**, not always on a mixed photo+shape until you convert/careful-select.
mistakes: - Stretching a photo so faces look wide — hold Shift or lock ratio.
- Saving a document without the image folder when images were linked, not embedded.

qa.q: Name any four text-wrapping options in Writer.
qa.a: None, Before, After, Parallel, Optimal, Through, In Background (any four).

qa.q: What does grouping do?
qa.a: It joins selected drawing objects so they move, resize and copy as a single object.

qa.q: Explain anchoring of images in Writer.
qa.a: Anchor decides what the image sticks to: **To Paragraph** (moves with the para), **To Character**, **As Character** (in the text line), **To Page** (fixed on that page). Choose To Paragraph + Optimal wrap for reports.

qa.q: An image covers the heading of a report. Which two settings would you change first?
qa.a: Wrap (Optimal or After) and arrangement (Send to Back) or move the anchor to the correct paragraph.

A student’s picture sits in a huge white box and the caption is not numbered.

(a) Two likely causes.
(b) Steps to insert a proper Figure caption.
(c) Why captions help in a long file.
a: (a) Wrap = None; image as a huge As-Character object; no Insert Caption used.
(b) Right-click → Insert Caption → category Figure → type the title.
(c) Auto numbering and a Table of Figures.

title: ToC, Templates and Track Changes
short: Table of Contents, templates, track changes, comments and mail merge.
lede: The rest of Writer. ToC from Heading styles, a template `.ott`, and review tools.
lens: ToC steps and Track Changes on/off are asked every year.
Mail merge: data source + main document + merge fields.
concepts: **1. Table of Contents:** apply Heading 1/2/3 → Insert → Table of Contents and Index → Table of Contents. Update with right-click → **Update Index** after edits.
**2. Template (`.ott`):** a starter document with styles, headers, logos. File → Templates → Save as Template. File → New → Templates to use it.
**3. Track Changes:** Edit → Track Changes → Record. Insertions show as underline, deletions as strike-out. Accept or Reject from the toolbar. Useful when two people edit one file.
**4. Comments:** Insert → Comment (`Ctrl+Alt+C`) for notes in the margin without changing the text.
**5. Mail Merge:** main letter + data source (Calc/Base/CSV) + merge fields (Name, Address) → Print or save letters. Steps: Tools → Mail Merge Wizard, or insert fields then File → Print → Mail Merge.
**6. Advantages of mail merge:** same letter to many people, no retyping, fewer spelling mistakes in names, labels and envelopes too.
steps: 2. Connect a data source (Calc sheet with Name, Address columns).
3. Insert merge fields where the name/address should appear.
4. Preview, then output to printer or separate files.
tricks: - Empty ToC ⇒ headings are not Heading styles.
- Track Changes must be **Record On** *before* the other person edits, or you will see no markup.
mistakes: - Saving a template as `.odt` instead of `.ott`.
- Typing names by hand in 50 letters instead of merge fields.

qa.q: Write the steps to insert a Table of Contents in Writer.
qa.a: Apply Heading styles → Insert → Table of Contents and Index → Table of Contents → OK. Right-click → Update Index after changes.

qa.q: What is a document template?
qa.a: A model file (`.ott`) that stores styles, headers and boilerplate so new documents start consistent.

qa.q: Explain mail merge and its advantages.
qa.a: Mail merge combines a main document with a data source to produce personalised letters. Advantages: speed, accuracy of names, one design for many copies, labels/envelopes.

qa.q: A teacher wants 40 identical permission letters with only the parent name changing. Which Writer feature, and what two files does she need?
qa.a: Mail merge. She needs the main letter and a data source (Calc column `ParentName`).
